title: `NULLS FIRST` / `NULLS LAST` are not tokenized as order keywords like `ASC` and `DESC`
spec:
This is the sqlparse library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`.

`ASC` and `DESC` are tokenized as `Token.Keyword.Order`, but the null ordering that belongs to the same sort specification is a plain `Token.Keyword`, so code that looks for order keywords misses it.

```python
import sqlparse
p = sqlparse.parse('DESC NULLS LAST')[0]
[(t.ttype, t.value) for t in p.tokens]
```
Expected: `[(Token.Keyword.Order, 'DESC NULLS LAST')]`
Actual: `[(Token.Keyword.Order, 'DESC'), (Token.Text.Whitespace, ' '), (Token.Keyword, 'NULLS LAST')]`

The rule: each of `ASC`, `DESC`, `NULLS FIRST`, `NULLS LAST`, `ASC NULLS FIRST`, `ASC NULLS LAST`, `DESC NULLS FIRST` and `DESC NULLS LAST` parsed on its own should be exactly one token of type `Token.Keyword.Order`. The same applies inside `ORDER BY`, e.g. `SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY a DESC NULLS LAST`.
acceptance: Each of the eight listed forms parses to a single `Token.Keyword.Order` token
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
